originalTitle: Trump warns of return to ‘strong military action’ if Iran diplomacy fails
summary: Washington and Tehran issue conflicting messages over the status of talks to end Middle East crisis
content: Donald Trump has once again warned that the US will return to “strong military action” against Iran if diplomatic efforts do not bring a rapid resolution to the crisis in the Middle East. “We are in very deep talks with Iran. If they don’t work out, we will go back to very strong military action,” the US president told Axios on Monday. Asked for how long he would allow the talks to proceed, he answered: “Not much time. Either it goes fast or not at all.” He reiterated the line to reporters later the same day on Air Force One. “They want to meet, and we’re meeting. Without what we did, they wouldn’t even be talking to us … They would not have requested the meeting if we were doing poorly. The only reason they want to meet is because we’ve been hitting them very hard.” He doubled down at a rally in Michigan soon after. “You ⁠can’t bribe them. You’ve ‌got ‌to beat them, ‌and we’ll beat the hell out of them. But we’ll ‌see how it turns out,” he said . “Right now, ⁠there are very friendly negotiations going on.” Earlier, Tehran said there were no direct talks with the US to end the conflict, which began in late February with a wave of US-Israeli strikes and has rocked the region and the global economy. “Mediators may convey messages from the American side to us regarding current developments in the region. But at present we are not engaged in any negotiations with the United States,” said the Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei. The diplomatic back and forth came as Oman and Iran drew closer to an agreement in principle on the future management of the strait of Hormuz, but remained unable to resolve Tehran’s demand that all ships passing through the strategic waterway must pay some type of transit fee or toll to a consortium led by the two countries. Oman and Iran met for technical talks in Tehran on Friday and Saturday that may hold the key to preventing a further round of fighting. Perceived progress in the talks – backed by China, Qatar and Pakistan – was understood to have fed into the US decision to pause its attacks on Iran after nearly two weeks. Senior US officials are also reported to have warned Trump over dwindling US munitions stockpiles and the impact of Iranian reprisals on US bases in the region, including Kuwait and Jordan. The top US military commander in the Middle East, Adm Brad Cooper, reportedly recommended stopping the bombing campaign around the strait because it had reached the limit of its effectiveness. The US attacks have been described by Washington as a response to repeated Iranian breaches of the memorandum of understanding signed in June, including by trying to prevent commercial shipping from transiting the strait through a southern route overseen by the US. Iran argues the southern route breaks the ceasefire agreement, which it insists left the country in sole charge of how the strait was reopened. A diplomat said: “The aim of the Tehran talks is to marry the Iran and Oman proposals so what emerges is clearly compliant with the law of the sea, and internationally acceptable.” At a Tehran press conference, Baqaei denied that the pause in US fighting amounted to an informal ceasefire. Oman has been trying since May to persuade Tehran that any plan for charging fees in the strait must be voluntary, to comply with the law of the sea. It has proposed a model similar to that which governs the strait of Malacca: countries that use it voluntarily contribute to a fund that provides for environmental and safety services to shipping. Oman argues that a similar entity could be set up in the strait of Hormuz with the agreement of the UN and the International Maritime Organization. The IMO secretary general, Arsenio Dominguez, has told the Guardian that the Malacca strait model is worth considering for the strait of Hormuz. Iran’s department of environment has drafted its own plan, under which “the annual passage of over 50,000 ships and oil tankers through the strait of Hormuz and their role in polluting the Persian Gulf” must be compensated for. Under the plan, Iran would be able to collect “fees” from passing vessels proportional to the type of ship, cargo volume, navigation history and history of pollution. The comparison between the straits of Malacca and Hormuz is imperfect since fewer ships see ports in the Malacca strait as a destination point. But the Iranian media appear increasingly drawn to the Malacca model. The Khabaronline news agency argued such an agreement would be “a win-win situation for Iran”. Baqaei described the talks with Oman as useful and constructive but said they had nothing to do with the US. “The goal is for Iran and Oman, as two coastal states, to develop mechanisms to ensure safe shipping in the strait of Hormuz, while respecting the sovereign rights of the two coastal states and also preserving Iran’s security and national interests,” he said. Oman is in a tight spot since it knows the US is opposed to the introduction of tolls, but it may accept a very clearly delineated system of fees for specific services. The talks come as the US continues to encourage commercial shipping to test the strength of the Iranian blockade of the strait. Iranian officials reported that six vessels with their navigation systems switched off attempted to pass through the southern route of the strait on Sunday. One of them was fired upon and the others were turned back to the Persian Gulf. The US has reimposed a blockade of Iranian oil exports and ended a sanctions waiver on its oil exports. The United Nations Office for Project Services said on Monday that transits through the strait of Hormuz had fallen to an average of approximately five ships a day over the past week, compared with nearly 130 a day before the war.
chineseTitle: 特朗普警告称，如果伊朗外交失败，将恢复“强有力的军事行动”
chineseSummary: 华盛顿和德黑兰就结束中东危机的谈判状况发出相互矛盾的信息
chineseContent: 唐纳德·特朗普再次警告称，如果外交努力不能迅速解决中东危机，美国将重新对伊朗采取“强有力的军事行动”。 “我们正在与伊朗进行非常深入的谈判。如果谈判不成功，我们将重新采取非常强有力的军事行动，”美国总统周一告诉 Axios。当被问及他允许谈判进行多长时间时，他回答说：“时间不多。要么进展快，要么根本不进行。”当天晚些时候，他在空军一号上向记者重申了这句话。 “他们想要会面，我们正在会面。如果没有我们所做的事情，他们甚至不会和我们说话……如果我们做得不好，他们就不会要求会面。他们想要会面的唯一原因是因为我们一直在严厉打击他们。”不久之后，他在密歇根州的一次集会上加倍努力。 “你不能贿赂他们。你必须打败他们，我们会把他们打败。但我们会看看结果如何，”他说。 “目前，正在进行非常友好的谈判。”早些时候，德黑兰表示，没有与美国进行直接谈判来结束这场冲突。这场冲突始于二月底，美国和以色列发起了一波袭击，震动了该地区和全球经济。 “调解员可能会向我们传达美方有关该地区当前事态发展的信息。但目前我们没有与美国进行任何谈判，”伊朗外交部发言人伊斯梅尔·巴卡伊表示。外交上的来来回回正值阿曼和伊朗接近就霍尔木兹海峡的未来管理达成原则协议，但仍无法解决德黑兰的要求，即所有经过战略水道的船只必须向两国牵头的财团支付某种类型的过境费或通行费。阿曼
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
